problem.symptom: On the installed v23 the media volume slider does nothing. The framework's own index is 0 and STREAM_MUSIC reports Muted: true, yet the speaker plays at full scale. Every stream behaves the same way; media is just the one that is noticed.
problem.cause: The audio policy configuration on this device comes from the AIDL HAL, and so does the engine configuration. The HAL parses Xiaomi's engine XML, which declares eight device categories AOSP does not define (DEVICE_CATEGORY_A2DP, DEVICE_CATEGORY_USB and their CE and SPATIALIZER_CE variants), 33 curves in all beside the 60 standard ones. The xsdc parser maps an unknown enumeration to UNKNOWN, aidl2legacy_DeviceCategory refuses that value, and because the AIDL path converts volume groups with convertContainer(), the first refusal discards the entire engine configuration. EngineBase then falls back to gDefaultEngineConfig, whose volumeGroups list is empty, so processParsingResult() builds one volume group per default strategy from a default-constructed configuration with no curve points at all. VolumeCurves::volIndexToDb() returns 0.0f when it holds no curve for the device category, so every index maps to no attenuation. AudioService mutes a stream by setting index 0, which is why index 0 is the loudest setting rather than silence.

evidence.hal_parsed_the_xml: AHAL_Config: getEngineConfig: number of strategies parsed: 8, default strategy: 5, number of volume groups parsed: 12
evidence.conversion_failure: APM::AudioPolicyEngine/Config: Function: aidl2legacy_AudioHalVolumeCurve_VolumeCurve Line: 143 Failed result (BAD_VALUE) -> aidl2legacy_AudioHalVolumeGroup_VolumeGroup Line: 156 -> APM::AudioPolicyEngine/Base: loadAudioPolicyEngineConfig: There was an error parsing AIDL data
evidence.curveless_groups: APM::AudioPolicyEngine/Base: processParsingResult: No configuration of AUDIO_STREAM_MUSIC found, using default volume configuration (repeated for all fifteen default groups)
evidence.runtime_effect: APM::VolumeCurve: Invalid device category 1 for Volume Curve, logged from VolumeCurves::volIndexToDb() on every volume computation
evidence.dump: dumpsys media.audio_policy prints every volume group with its stream, attributes and index range and not one curve point
evidence.xiaomi_categories: /odm/etc/audio_policy_engine_stream_volumes_mi.xml declares 12 DEVICE_CATEGORY_A2DP, 12 DEVICE_CATEGORY_USB, 2 each of DEVICE_CATEGORY_A2DP_CE, DEVICE_CATEGORY_HEADSET_CE and DEVICE_CATEGORY_USB_CE, and 1 each of the three SPATIALIZER_CE variants, alongside 12 curves for each of the five AOSP categories

fix.mechanism: When the converted HAL engine configuration has no volume groups, fill them from the legacy volume tables before building the engine, exactly as the XML path does when it finds no engine configuration at all. The AIDL conversion itself is left upstream, so the product strategies stay the AOSP defaults.
fix.result_expected: Every volume group is built with the curves in /vendor/etc/audio_policy_volumes.xml and default_volume_tables.xml, whose group names (AUDIO_STREAM_MUSIC and the rest) are exactly the names the default product strategies reference, so every stream attenuates again.
fix.scope: One function in the audio policy engine. No HAL, SELinux, vendor or identity change, and no change to which product strategies the framework uses.

safety.product_strategies_unchanged: the AIDL conversion still fails exactly as upstream, so the engine keeps the AOSP default strategies that v23 boots with
safety.duplicate_stream_check: processParsingResult() aborts if a legacy stream is assigned to two volume groups. The legacy tables name one group per stream type, which is what the default strategies expect.

remaining: On-device confirmation that the media slider attenuates and that index 0 is silent
The curves now come from the AOSP legacy tables, not from Xiaomi's tuned per-category ones, so absolute levels will not match stock exactly
Ring, alarm, notification and call volumes were broken the same way and need the same check

superseded_attempt.what_it_did: also patched EngineConfig.cpp to skip volume curves whose device category the framework cannot represent, so the whole HAL engine configuration was accepted instead of discarded
superseded_attempt.why_it_was_wrong: accepting the configuration also adopted the HAL product strategies, which come from Xiaomi's /odm/etc/audio_policy_engine_product_strategies_mi.xml and declare usages the framework cannot expose (AUDIO_USAGE_BLUETOOTH_SCO and the three deprecated NOTIFICATION_COMMUNICATION_* ones)

superseded_attempt.lesson: the volume groups and the product strategies arrive in the same payload, and only the volume groups are safe to take from this HAL
